item.title: Anti-Environmentalism and the Future of Green Growth
item.content:encoded:
Luca Gori, University of Pisa

Simone Marsiglio, University of Pisa

Anastasios Xepapadeas, Athens University of Economics and Business

This special issue addresses the growing political and social opposition to environmental regulation and climate mitigation efforts, examining how anti-environmentalism affects green growth and sustainable development. The collection investigates the drivers and implications of anti-environmental attitudes, considering how economic incentives, institutional factors, and policy design interact with public resistance to environmental policies.

The special issue welcomes research from environmental economics, macroeconomics, political economy, and behavioral economics that explores the relationship between anti-environmentalism and sustainable growth. It seeks comprehensive analysis of mechanisms through which opposition to environmental policies operates and how economic systems can progress toward green growth despite political polarization and societal backlash.

The collection prioritizes methodological contributions—theoretical, empirical, or experimental—that illuminate the complex interactions between anti-environmental movements and green growth. Both participants and non-participants of the related HEDGE conference are encouraged to submit high-quality papers on these topics.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Economic, social and political determinants of anti-environmental attitudes and behavior
  • Impact of populism, misinformation, and lobbying on climate and environmental policy
  • Public perception and resistance to carbon taxation, green industrial policies, and regulation
  • Distributional and equity aspects of green growth as sources of policy backlash
  • Role of institutions and governance in shaping environmental resistance
  • International and comparative analyses of anti-environmental movements and climate cooperation
  • Behavioral and cultural dimensions of environmental skepticism and pro-growth narratives
  • Policy strategies for overcoming anti-environmentalist sentiment and fostering green transitions
  • Economic growth under climate-related extreme event risk and costs of climate skepticism

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Valuing health and longevity: Advances and innovations
item.content:encoded:
Olof Bystrom, OECD

Ståle Navrud, Norwegian University of Life Sciences

Lisa A. Robinson, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

Mortality risk valuations are central to assessing the benefits of environmental policies, but the research base on value per statistical life contains significant gaps and inconsistencies. There is insufficient evidence on how population characteristics and risk properties influence these values, and synthesizing results across studies remains challenging. Nonfatal health impacts, while often substantial, receive comparatively less research attention and are frequently valued using indirect cost-based approaches rather than direct willingness-to-pay measures.

The collection addresses emerging research that tackles these limitations through improved valuation methodologies for both mortality and morbidity risks, refined techniques for combining and transferring estimates across contexts, and innovations addressing equity considerations in benefit assessment. This special issue serves as a reference for researchers and practitioners working on the economic valuation of health effects in environmental policy analysis.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Value per statistical life (VSL)
  • Willingness to pay (WTP) for mortality risk reductions
  • Nonfatal risk reductions and morbidity valuation
  • Population and risk attributes affecting valuations
  • Benefit transfer and meta-analysis methods
  • Health impact economic valuation
  • Environmental policy benefit estimation
  • Equity and distributional concerns in valuation
  • Best practice approaches for health valuation

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Submission deadline
